To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we demonstrate a global feedback architecture that integrates a high-order PWM Class-D amplifier in a deep-submicron CMOS process and achieve the highest output power and best THD+N performance reported to date.
a global feedback mixed-signal Class-D audio amplifier is implemented in 55 nm digital CMOS and attains a high SNR and low THD+N.

the use of global closed-loop digital control in a mixed-signal Class-D architecture is compatible with deep submicron process technologies and can achieve performance that is competitive with conventional analog designs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and analysis of a global closed-loop Class-D amplifier architecture and the implementation of a prototype in a 55 nm CM OS.
the development of a high performance, mixed signal architecture and the design of a fourth-order Class-D audio amplifier in deep-submicrometers CMOS.

the challenges of implementing high performance audio amplifiers using deep-submicron CMOS and the proposed mixed-signal architecture is shown to overcome these challenges and achieve performance competitive with traditional approaches.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed architecture and design methodology is an attractive alternative for high performance Class-D audio amplification in deep-submicrons.
this paper reports the first demonstration of an integrated high performance audio amplifier in a deep-submicron CMOS technology.
the proposed architecture and methodology is the most efficient and scalable solution for implementing high-performance Class-D amplifiers in deep-submicrons.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
this paper introduces a new paradigm for high-order Class-D audio amplifier design and demonstrates that the proposed architecture is a practical alternative for deep-submicrons CMOS.
the proposed architecture can be implemented in scaled CMOS and is therefore a viable solution for high-performance audio amplifier designs.
this design is a significant step towards the realization of a fully integrated, high performance audio amplifier in deep-submicrons.

global digital control and mixed-signal feedback loop design can significantly improve the performance of Class-D audio amplification in advanced CMOS. © 2013 IEEE.
